title: Blink
description: The classic: an LED on D13 (through 220 Ω on a breadboard) blinks once a second. It has a PCB too: an Uno shield — switch to PCB in the toolbar.

title: Button
description: A pushbutton from D2 to GND with the internal pull-up lights the LED on D13 while held.

title: Fade
description: analogWrite on D9 ramps an LED up and down with PWM.

title: Traffic light
description: Red, red + yellow, green, yellow — a traffic light on D10, D9 and D8, cycling every 2 s.

title: Simon game
description: Four buttons, four LEDs and a buzzer: repeat the growing sequence. Run it and press the buttons.

title: Serial echo
description: Type in the serial monitor (9600 baud): the Uno sends every byte straight back.

title: Potentiometer
description: analogRead(A0) of a potentiometer printed ten times a second — turn the knob.

title: Nano on a breadboard
description: An Arduino Nano straddles a breadboard and reads two potentiometers on A6 and A7 — analog-only pins the Uno lacks. Turn the knobs; watch Serial or the Plotter.

title: Logic analyzer demo
description: SoftwareSerial on D3, PWM on D9 and a 1 kHz square wave on D7: probe them with the Probe tool.

title: LCD 16×2
description: LiquidCrystal in 4-bit mode: "Hello, Benchtop!" and a seconds counter.

title: LCD 16×2 over I2C
description: The same text through a PCF8574 backpack at 0x27; the backlight goes off at 1.5 s.

title: LCD thermometer
description: A DHT22 read every 2 s, temperature and humidity on an I2C LCD — change them with its sliders.

title: OLED (SSD1306)
description: Adafruit_SSD1306 draws a border, text and a circle on a 128×64 I2C OLED.

title: OLED clock
description: A DS1307 real-time clock shown large on an SSD1306 OLED, and printed every second.

title: Color TFT (ILI9341)
description: A 240×320 ILI9341 on hardware SPI, driven by a small driver in the sketch itself: colored boxes, a title, and a counter that redraws only its digit.

title: 7-segment display
description: A 4-digit display multiplexed at ~120 Hz shows "1234".

title: LED bar graph
description: Ten LEDs on D11…D2, six of them lit.

title: NeoPixel strip and ring
description: 24 WS2812 pixels — a strip chained into a ring — bit-banged from D6.

title: Temperature and humidity (DHT22)
description: Adafruit's DHT library reads a DHT22 every 2.1 s — change its sliders.

title: Ultrasonic distance (HC-SR04)
description: pulseIn times the echo and prints the distance in cm, ten times a second.

title: Distance meter
description: An HC-SR04 measured five times a second, the distance in cm on a 4-digit 7-segment display.

title: Real-time clock (DS1307)
description: Sets the clock to just before midnight and prints the time every second.

title: Accelerometer (MPU-6050)
description: Raw I2C reads of acceleration, temperature and rotation.

title: IR remote
description: Press the remote’s keys while it runs: an IR receiver on D2 turns them into NEC frames, and a small decoder in the sketch prints each key (and "repeat" while you hold one).

title: Kitchen scale (HX711)
description: A load cell through an HX711, read by a shift-in in the sketch: it tares at start, then prints grams twice a second — set the weight in the Inspector.

title: Flame alarm
description: A flame sensor module: raise the infrared in the Inspector past the trimmer’s threshold and the buzzer sounds; the sketch prints each change with the analog reading.

title: Gas meter (MQ-2)
description: An MQ-2 module prints its analog reading four times a second and raises an alarm past the threshold — set the gas concentration in ppm in the Inspector.

title: Keypad 4×4
description: A matrix keypad scanned row by row; each key press is printed.

title: Rotary encoder (KY-040)
description: Counts detents up and down and reports shaft presses.

title: Servo sweep
description: Servo.h sweeps a servo from 0° to 180° and back in 5° steps.

title: Servo knob
description: A potentiometer steers a servo: turn the knob in the Inspector while it runs.

title: Keypad lock
description: Type 1 2 3 4 # on the keypad: the servo latch opens for 3 s; a wrong code beeps.

title: Stepper (28BYJ-48)
description: Stepper.h turns a 28BYJ-48 on a ULN2003 driver a quarter turn at a time.

title: A4988 stepper driver
description: An A4988 on STEP/DIR turns a bipolar stepper one turn in full steps, then one turn back in sixteenth steps — watch the shaft move in fine increments.

title: Relay
description: D7 switches a relay coil every 500 ms; its contact lights an LED.

title: Gas alarm with a fan
description: A gas leak opens near an MQ-2: past the alarm level the buzzer sounds and an extractor fan on D7 runs until the air is clean again. Switch the leak in the Inspector; the heatmap shows the gas spreading.

title: PIR hallway light
description: A person walks down a hallway past a PIR sensor: the lamp on D8 lights while they are in view and goes off a second after they leave.

title: Parking sensor
description: A car drives toward an HC-SR04: the beeps come faster as it closes in, and a steady tone says STOP below 30 cm.

title: Thermostat
description: An NTC reads the room and D7 switches a heater to hold 25 °C with half a degree of hysteresis; the heatmap shows the warm air.

title: Buzzers
description: tone() plays 440 Hz then 880 Hz on a passive buzzer; an active one beeps after. Unmute to hear them.

title: Speaker melody
description: tone() plays three notes on a speaker on D8 — through your computer’s speakers once you unmute.

title: PCM through PWM
description: A 1 kHz sine as 8 kHz samples in Timer2’s 62.5 kHz PWM on D3; the speaker filters the carrier away.

title: Microphone pitch
description: A microphone on A0; the sketch prints the pitch it hears every 500 ms. Run, select the mic, click “Use microphone” and whistle.

title: VU meter
description: A microphone and a 10-LED bar graph: the louder it hears, the more bars light. Try “Use microphone”.

title: ESP32 blink
description: An ESP32 DevKit V1 blinks an LED on D2 (and its onboard LED) through FreeRTOS.

title: ESP32 serial hello
description: A full dual-core boot on the real ROM, then "hello from esp32" at 115200 baud.

title: ESP32 button
description: A button on D4 with INPUT_PULLUP lights the LED on D2 while held.

title: ESP32 PWM fader
description: A potentiometer on GPIO34 (ADC1) sets an LED’s brightness through LEDC PWM.

title: ESP32 NeoPixel
description: neopixelWrite through the RMT peripheral: red, green, blue, dim white.

title: ESP32 rainbow ring
description: A turning rainbow on a 16-pixel NeoPixel ring, sent bit by bit through the RMT peripheral.

title: ESP32 OLED clock
description: A DS1307 and an SSD1306 on the ESP32’s I2C: the time large on the OLED.

title: ESP32 color TFT
description: The same ILI9341 picture over the ESP32’s VSPI bus (SCK 18, MOSI 23), with CS on D5 and D/C on D4.

title: ESP32 DAC sine
description: dacWrite on GPIO25 steps a 500 Hz sine into a speaker (unmute to hear it).

title: ESP32 microphone pitch
description: A microphone on GPIO34 (ADC1); the sketch prints the pitch it hears every 500 ms.

title: ESP32 I2C scan
description: Wire scans the bus and finds the OLED (0x3C) and the clock (0x68).

title: Pico blink
description: The Raspberry Pi Pico on its own: the onboard LED (GP25) blinks every half second.

title: Pico potentiometer
description: analogRead of a potentiometer on GP26 (ADC0) at 12 bits, printed ten times a second on USB serial — turn the knob.

title: Pico PWM steps
description: analogWrite on GP15 at 1 kHz: an LED steps through 0, 25, 50, 75 and 100 % duty, 200 ms each.

title: Pico OLED
description: Adafruit SSD1306 over Wire on GP4 (SDA) and GP5 (SCL): a box, "PICO" and a seconds counter.

title: Pico color TFT
description: The ILI9341 picture over SPI0 (SCK GP18, MOSI GP19), with CS on GP17 and D/C on GP20, then a digit counter.

title: Pico NeoPixel
description: Eight WS2812 pixels on GP2 driven by a PIO program, not bit-banging: pixel 0 steps red, green, blue every half second.

title: MicroPython blink
description: MicroPython on the Pico: main.py toggles the LED every 250 ms and prints the count. Edit it in the Code tab and press Run — nothing to compile.

title: MicroPython NeoPixel
description: MicroPython's neopixel module drives the WS2812 strip on GP2: pixel 0 steps red, green, blue every half second.

title: Pico PIO square wave
description: A two-instruction PIO program toggles GP3 at exactly 10 kHz while the CPU sleeps: probe GP3 with the Probe tool.

title: Pico dual core
description: Both cores at work: setup()/loop() blink the onboard LED every half second while setup1()/loop1() blink GP15 twice as fast; the cores trade numbers through the inter-core FIFO and print them.

title: Pico 2 blink
description: The Raspberry Pi Pico 2 on its own: the RP2350's RISC-V cores boot through the real bootrom and blink the onboard LED (GP25) every half second.

title: Pico 2 potentiometer
description: analogRead of a potentiometer on GP26 (ADC0) at 12 bits, printed ten times a second on USB serial — turn the knob.

title: Pico 2 PWM steps
description: analogWrite on GP15 at 1 kHz: an LED steps through 0, 25, 50, 75 and 100 % duty, 200 ms each.

title: Pico 2 OLED
description: Adafruit SSD1306 over Wire on GP4 (SDA) and GP5 (SCL): a box, "PICO" and a seconds counter.

title: Pico 2 color TFT
description: The ILI9341 picture over SPI0 (SCK GP18, MOSI GP19), with CS on GP17 and D/C on GP20, then a digit counter.

title: Pico 2 NeoPixel
description: Eight WS2812 pixels on GP2 driven by the RP2350's PIO: pixel 0 steps red, green, blue every half second.

title: Pico 2 MicroPython blink
description: MicroPython on the Pico 2's RISC-V cores: main.py toggles the LED every 250 ms and prints the count. Edit it in the Code tab and press Run — nothing to compile.

title: Pico 2 button interrupt
description: A pushbutton on GP14 with the internal pull-up; attachInterrupt counts presses and prints them on USB serial — press it.

title: Mega LED chaser
description: Ten LEDs on the Mega’s odd pins D23–D41 light one after another, there and back — one shared resistor, since one LED is lit at a time.

title: Mega serial ports
description: The Mega has four UARTs: Serial1–3 are each wired back to themselves (TX→RX), and Serial reports what every port heard.

title: Mega analog scanner
description: All 16 analog inputs read ten times a second; four potentiometers on A0, A5, A8 and A15 — turn them, or watch the Plotter.

title: Uno ↔ ESP32 chat
description: The Uno sends "ping n" through a 5 V → 3.3 V divider; the ESP32 answers "pong n" on its TX2; both serial monitors show the chat.

title: Uno → ESP32 relay
description: The Uno pings ten times a second; the ESP32 copies what its Serial2 hears to its own serial monitor.
